subject: [Invite] Engineer onboarding webinar — RSVP friction reduction & seat allocation
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Paula Reyes <paula@acme.dev>, devops-team@acme.dev
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: [Invite] Engineer onboarding webinar — RSVP friction reduction & seat allocation

Hi Paula / Acme devops team,

Following up on our brief at KubeCon — we’re running a 45-minute live workshop next month specifically for engineering teams migrating inference workloads. Goal: show a short migration checklist, a live demo of our private deployment flow, and a simple cost/latency tuning checklist you can apply in an afternoon.

We want to make the sign-up low-friction for engineers (no long forms, timezone-aware slots, and immediate calendar adds). Quick ask: would you prefer a single 45-minute session or staggered 30-minute sessions targeted at timezone lanes?

Proposed times (PST):
- Wed Oct 20 — 11:00–11:45 (single session)
- Wed Oct 20 — staggered: 10:00–10:30 / 12:00–12:30 / 16:00–16:30 (3 small sessions)

We’ll hold a small number of reserved seats for Acme (5 per lane) if you’d like priority access. RSVP link and tracking will be shared — we can rotate CTAs for your internal lists to measure lift.

Attaching: agenda + tracking link CSV (we’ll populate with UTM variants once you confirm).

Thanks — happy to adapt.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Field Marketing, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood-webinar-agenda-deck.pdf (Agenda; 2 slides), rsvp-tracking-links-rotation.csv (stub)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paula Reyes <paula@acme.dev>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Invite] Engineer onboarding webinar — RSVP friction reduction & seat allocation

On Tue, Sep 21, 2026 at 3:02 PM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Following up on our brief at KubeCon — we’re running a 45-minute live workshop next month specifically for engineering teams migrating inference workloads.

Sean — quick ops note: smaller sessions reduce dropoff in our past cohorts (esp. APAC/EMEA distribution), but increase orchestration overhead. If Acme wants reserved seats, we should flag: 1) calendar invite auto-add (yes/no), 2) single-click RSVP vs. form + company validation.

I recommend: offer 3 lanes (AM/Noon/PM) with single-click RSVP and an optional short link to select preferred demo focus (on-prem vs. hosted). I’ll prepare the tracking CSV with three UTM variants and a HubSpot campaign id.

Also: proposed subject lines to A/B test — I’ll add in the doc.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Field Marketing Ops, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
From: Daniel Park <daniel@acme.dev>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paula Reyes <paula@acme.dev>, devops-team@acme.dev
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Invite] Engineer onboarding webinar — RSVP friction reduction & seat allocation

Thanks Sean — this looks good. Short answers from Acme:
- Prefer staggered 30-minute lanes (makes it easier for on-call rotations).
- Yes to reserved seats (5 per lane) — Paula will confirm names after we finalize the time.
- Single-click RSVP preferred; don’t need additional form fields.

Can you confirm whether the RSVP will auto-add to calendar by default (we prefer yes)? And can you provide one tracking link we can drop into our internal Slack channel and one with an email UTM for Paula’s distribution?

—Daniel
Senior Platform Engineer, Acme Dev
daniel@acme.dev
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@acme.dev>, Paula Reyes <paula@acme.dev>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Invite] Engineer onboarding webinar — RSVP friction reduction & seat allocation

On Thu, Sep 23, 2026 at 11:26 AM Daniel Park <daniel@acme.dev> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether the RSVP will auto-add to calendar by default (we prefer yes)?

Hi Daniel — yes, RSVP is single-click and creates an ICS calendar add. We’ll supply two short links: one for Slack/internal drop (no UTM), and one for the email invite with UTM_campaign=acme_engineer_onboard. Sample links below — I’ll replace these with HubSpot-tracked URLs when we publish: 
- Slack short link (no UTM): https://rbw.io/r/slack-acme-engineer
- Email tracked link: https://rbw.io/r/track?link=acme_engineer&utm_campaign=acme_engineer_onboard

I’ll attach the CSV with the three UTM variants and the subject line A/B pairs. We’ll reserve 5 seats per lane and maintain a waitlist; if a reserved attendee does not confirm by 48 hours before the session, we’ll release the seat to the waitlist.

Deliverables timeline: 
- Monday Sep 27: final RSVP links + CSV, subject A/B list, calendar invite templates.
- Wed Oct 6: first reminder email to registered attendees (24–48 hours before).

—Mateo
Senior Event Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@acme.dev>, Paula Reyes <paula@acme.dev>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Invite] Engineer onboarding webinar — RSVP friction reduction & seat allocation

Thanks Daniel — all sounds good. Quick logistics recap so Paula can loop in whomever needs access: 
- Final: staggered 30-minute lanes on Wed Oct 20 (10:00, 12:00, 16:00 PST).
- Reserved: 5 seats per lane for Acme; we’ll hold them until 48 hours before each lane.
- RSVP behavior: single-click, auto-add to calendar (ICS), immediate confirmation email + link to join.
- Tracking: Slack short link + email UTM link. Attached are the agenda deck and CSV for tracking/rotation.

Paula — if you confirm names for the reserved seats, I’ll mark them in HubSpot and create a private pre-registered list that bypasses the public waitlist.

See attachments.

—Sean
